newsitem.title: USA: MHC's new bid pressures Chateau.
newsitem.headline: MHC's new bid pressures Chateau.

text.p: Manufactured Home Communities Inc's offer on Wednesday to sweeten its bid for Chateau Properties Inc will put more pressure on Chateau to negotiate with its fellow mobile home park operator, analysts said.
"It places additional obligation on Chateau to consider this instead of just charging ahead," said Burland East, an analyst for EVEREN Securities.
MHC chairman Sam Zell said in a letter to Chateau that MHC was prepared to include a tax-deferred option for operating partnership (OP) unit holders and an enhanced cash offer.
The offer is subject to a meeting between the two companies this week and a negotiated agreement. MHC said it previously has not had a dialogue with Chateau.
"The board will consider it," Jeff Kellogg, president and chief executive of Chateau, said in an interview..

Analysts said MHC might be able to raise its cash bid to $27 from the current tender offer of $26. According to MHC, as of Tuesday it controls about 51 percent of Chateau's outstanding shares -- a number that surprised most analysts as less than they had expected.
"I don't think much more than $27 would make sense," said William Acheson, a real estate investment trust analyst for Smith Barney.

"When you start getting to levels that high, it really provides a strong impetus for OP unit holders to convert. If all of a sudden you have a significant portion of nine million OP holders tendering, it raises the cost of any buyout significantly," he said.
Chateau and ROC Communities Inc last month agreed to a revised merger, allowing for a tax-deferred option for OP unit holders and an enhanced Chateau shareholder stock swap.
The two companies initially signed an agreement to merge in July.
"It's absolutely the best deal for our shareholders," Kellogg said.
Chateau has called its agreement with ROC "a merger of equals" and said the company is not for sale. But most analysts said the merger puts the company on the selling block.

"Any time a company says it's going to undergo a change of control, it has to consider all options," East said. "My guess is the management of Chateau and ROC have really come to know each other.... They view Sam (Zell) as a third wheel."

Even with the stepped-up pressure for negotiation, analysts largely agree the fight for the Chateau will ultimately be settled in court. MHC and Chateau have both filed suits against each other, and a class action suit was also filed against Chateau.
"The highest probability is this working its way through the courts," said Green Street Advisors analyst Jim Sullivan.
